input: head is None or the first node of a finite, acyclic singly linked list of n distinct node objects, with 0 <= n <= 4294967295. Each caller-owned ListNode has ordinary writable data fields val and next; val is an integer in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], and next is another node or None. No getters, proxies, custom assignment behavior or concurrent observers/mutations are allowed. External aliases may point at any input node and observe the final rewiring. Node values must be in nondecreasing order. Integers are plain int values, excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists rather than subclasses; strings are ordinary str values. Standard built-ins are unmodified and no concurrent mutation occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The list of exactly those original nodes whose value occurs once in the entire input, in their original relative order. All occurrences of a repeated value are excluded, rather than retaining one representative. Return None if no unique node remains.
mutation_aliasing: Values and identities are preserved. Only the private sentinel next and next fields of retained unique nodes can be written to bypass repeated runs. Removed nodes own next fields are not changed; external aliases into a removed chain may still reach retained nodes whose later links changed. Removed nodes are not destroyed or globally detached. The returned list contains each retained original node once and terminates at None without cycles. The sentinel is not returned; no output node is copied. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Values are compared for equality only; no arithmetic transformation occurs. The traversal uses node identity to distinguish a one-node run from a longer equal-value run. No sentinel numeric value can collide with a real node value.
complexity: O(n + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space, including one sentinel. Each maximal equal-value run is scanned once, and before advances only across retained singletons. No recursion, set, sorting or output-node allocation is used.
